# Overview

Canopy Height Models (CHM) represent vertical distance from ground to canopy top across the landscape. CHMs derived from normalized LiDAR point clouds serve as primary inputs for tree detection, biomass estimation, and forest inventory. This chapter documents operational workflows for CHM aggregation, mosaicking across multiple operating areas, and quality control procedures.

**Note:** CHMs are generated at 1m resolution during point cloud processing (Chapter 1: Point Clouds), then aggregated to match field plot scale (typically 100m).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.1 Prepare CHM

Create 1m resolution CHM from normalized point clouds using triangulation.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| error: false
#| echo: false
#| eval: false
# Generate 1m CHM
chm_1m <- lidR::grid_canopy(las_norm, res = 1, dsmtin(max_edge = 8))
plot(chm_1m, col = height.colors(50))
```

![](/assets/PNG/stem_detect_F.png){width="100%"}

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.2 Extract Dominant Height

### Point Cloud Extraction

Extract dominant height directly from point clouds without rasterizing. This method is slower but preserves full point information.

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Create a 1m grid
grid    	 = sf::st_make_grid(ttops_sf, cellsize = 1, square = TRUE)
grid_sf    = sf::st_sf(grid_id = 1:length(grid), geometry = grid)
ttops_grid = sf::st_join(ttops_sf, grid_sf)

ttops_95h  = ttops_grid |> 
	sf::st_drop_geometry() |> 
	dplyr::group_by(grid_id) |>
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    `95thQuantile` = quantile(Z, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max = max(Z, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) |>
  right_join(grid_sf, by = "grid_id") %>%
  sf::st_as_sf()

# Convert to raster if needed
ttops_95h_rast <- rasterize(
  vect(ttops_95h), 
  rast(ext(ttops_95h), res = 1, crs = crs(ttops_95h)),
  field = "95thQuantile"
)


# Plot
plot(ttops_95h_rast, main = "95th Percentile Height")
```

![](/assets/PNG/stem_detect_G.png)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Raster Extraction

Aggregate 1m CHM tiles to 30m resolution using 95th percentile statistics. This method is faster for large catalogs.

```{r}
#| eval: false

# Define 95th percentile function
quant95 <- function(x, ...) {
    quantile(x, probs = 0.95, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Aggregate 1m pixels to 30m using q95
chm_95h_30m <- terra::aggregate(
    chm_1m,
    fact = 30,
    fun = quant95
)

writeRaster(
    chm_95h_30m,
    filename = "./data/chm_95h_30m.tif",
    overwrite = TRUE
)
```

![](/assets/PNG/stem_detect_H.png)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.3 Validation

Compare 95th percentile CHM against detected tree heights from Chapter 2.

```{r}
#| eval: true

# Load stem detections and CHM
ttops <- sf::read_sf("../stem-detect/data/ttops_100m.gpkg")
chm_95h <- terra::rast("../stem-detect/data/chm_95h_30m.tif")

# Extract CHM values at tree locations
ttops$chm_95h <- terra::extract(chm_95h, vect(ttops))[, 2]

# Statistics
validation <- ttops %>%
    summarise(
        correlation = cor(Z, chm_95h, use = "complete.obs"),
        rmse = sqrt(mean((Z - chm_95h)^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
        mae = mean(abs(Z - chm_95h), na.rm = TRUE),
        bias = mean(Z - chm_95h, na.rm = TRUE)
    )

print(validation) # review and revise
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 3.4 Build Mosaic

Merge all operating areas into single product for Chapter 4

```{r}
#| eval: false

# List all area outputs
area_chms <- lapply(areas, function(a) {
    raster(sprintf("outputs/chm/chm_95h_100m.tif", a))
})

# Merge
chm_95h_final <- do.call(merge, c(area_chms, tolerance = 1))

# Save for biomass modeling
writeRaster(
    chm_95h_final,
    filename = "outputs/chm/chm_95h_100m_allAreas.tif",
    overwrite = TRUE
)
```

This raster is the dominant height input for biomass models in Chapter 4.
